The complete bundle was written, copied, hashed, and chmod 0444 before FIRST-READY was signaled to the coordinator. Only afterward were the frozen chapter and its input copies reread for this separate static review. No source changes were made after that freeze, and no revision bundle was needed.

Outcome: the first-ready chapter is the preferred whole deliverable. No packet mismatch was found by this static review. This conclusion is limited to inspection, with no runtime, compiler, lint, test, dependency implementation, or repository verification.

## Scope and API

The chapter begins with the factory export, contains the projection export, and ends after four private helpers. It contains no import, public type/interface preamble, new API, any type, suppression, exception translation, caching, retry, policy validation, or IO. All used free values and types are named in the packet/public API. The fallback connection has an explicit packet type, preserving literal typing without casts. Tuple entries and normalized models use the packet's ProviderId, ProviderConfig, and ModelId bindings.

## Async boundary

The callback is invoked directly as resolveConnections with an ordinary object whose fields evaluate configRevision, configuredProviders, and reasons in that order. Absent reasons create a fresh array, while supplied references are preserved. Neither previousProviders nor previousStates enters the callback argument. Await precedes configuration projection, and configuredProviders and previousProviders are reread afterward in the requested insertion order. No catch alters callback, thenable, projection, or state failure identity.

## Admission and configured projection

The index helper receives configuredProviders before connections, and fully indexes before configuredProviders.entries is called. Native Map.has reads providerId before admission; duplicate error interpolation reads it again. Nonduplicate configured lookup and final Map.set each independently read providerId. Error interpolation reads the ID only when that branch throws. Missing configuration uses truthiness, and account admission checks only access?.type. Every connection reference is retained without normalization.

Configured enumeration reads each access once, skips nonaccount configurations, and processes hidden account configurations identically. Exact configured providerId selects an indexed connection or a newly created unknown fallback. Every account configuration contributes one tuple, and the result is a new ProviderConfigMap without copied rule metadata.

## Configuration branches and models

Available is compared before pending; unavailable is compared only after both comparisons fail. Available/pending reads access.mode, and only start-plan reads connection.models. Normalization iterates values ?? [], calls value.trim with the original receiver, preserves order and duplicates, drops empty results, and freezes its fresh array including an empty array. Normalization completes before the final status read that determines entitled and before either constructor invocation.

Only access and the start-plan builtinModelIds whitelist enter newly created available/pending configurations. Unavailable reads neither previous/reset nor models and creates false entitlement. Remaining status reads resetPrevious first; a truthy reset skips input.previousProviders entirely. Otherwise it reads previousProviders.get(providerId), returns a truthy previous reference exactly, and creates a fresh false-entitlement configuration only when previous is falsy. No existing configuration or array is mutated or frozen by this code.

## State evaluation and preserved spread behavior

Original connections are traversed again in their own order. Previous-state lookup follows resetPrevious and uses an optional chain; provider lookup independently reads providerId afterward. Unavailable reason uses the packet's uncached status comparisons and truthy previous checks.

The ordinary states record uses direct indexed assignment, evaluating assignment-key providerId before the frozen object's RHS getters. The object evaluates native previous spread for unknown, then availability, strict entitled, conditional unavailableReason, conditional current, always-own connectionKey, and conditional effectiveAt in the required order. Comparison and value reads of current/effectiveAt are separate. Access entitlement is read after spread and availability and is true only for zhipu-account access with strict true entitlement.

Unknown native spread retains previous extra string/symbol fields, prior explicitly undefined reason fields, and previous current/effectiveAt when the new values are undefined. connectionKey is always overwritten, including with own undefined. Reset skips all previous state. Known statuses do not spread previous. Direct assignment preserves ordinary-object special-key/prototype behavior. The states record is frozen, then the returned ordinary object has providers before states and is frozen. Original connection/state objects are not frozen.

## Access and integration limits

Author reads were restricted to the two authorized packet files and own frozen chapter/input copies. Writes and artifact operations were restricted to the own author directory. FIRST-READY preceded this review. Hashing/freezing/file copying were artifact operations; the chapter was never run. The coordinator must install the entire chapter with the retained preamble and may apply formatting, then perform separately authorized integration/synthetic checks. Parent lane Sol/high Fast ON is reported verified/preserved; per-child Fast was not independently verified. Workspace isolation is self-enforced, and no cleanroom, novelty, license, rights, or mechanical-originality claim is made.
